item.title: UK Politics: Andy Burnham Theory of Growth Is Desperately Thin Stuff
item.description: Andy Burnham’s speech at the Labour Party’s annual conference was memorable. Unlike his predecessor, the new British prime minister sounded heartfelt and hopeful. And he took a few big swings at hard policies as well. Reform is promised for elderly care and Britain’s bloated welfare regime, as is a “national conversation” on the relationship with the European Union and the UK’s outdated winner-takes-all electoral system.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Sharma

item.title: Soaring Yields Find Europe’s Weak Spot in France
item.description: French bonds are tipping toward a full-blown crisis.
item.dc:creator: John Authers

item.title: Nike's China Reset Needs More Than the Kardashians
item.description: With Nike Inc.’s North American turnaround starting to take root, the sportswear giant can now devote more attention to tackling its biggest problem: China. But fixing the second-largest market means accepting that the business will be smaller and less profitable in the long run.
item.dc:creator: Juliana Liu

item.title: After the Anthropic IPO Comes the Dario Amodei Biopic
item.description: Lots of tech businesses have hit the brakes on going public in the second half of 2026, but not the company behind Claude.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Karl

item.title: Cheap Money Is History: The RBA Has a Blunt Warning on Rates
item.description: The Reserve Bank of Australia's interest-rate increase this week to the highest level in 15 years was a dress rehearsal for what's to come in bigger economies.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Moss

item.title: Hong Kong Investors Buying US Treasuries Is a No-Brainer
item.description: With its currency pegged to the US dollar, Hong Kong flinches when the Federal Reserve starts raising interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Shuli Ren

item.description: Performance fees, accredited investor tests, default shareholder voting and Knicks-Rangers deconglomeration.
item.dc:creator: Matt Levine

item.title: Trump's $54 Billion Election Pitch for Alaska LNG Is Its Undoing
item.description: President Donald Trump’s announcement on Wednesday that South Korea would invest $54 billion in a giant liquefied natural gas project in Alaska had a touch of the miraculous — as in, wondrous but tangential to reality. On Trump’s reading, Alaska LNG, having been little more than a pipe dream for decades, is now not only getting built, and with foreign money, but also secures its future just ahead of midterm elections by happy coincidence, and in a state with a tight, crucial Senate race, no less
item.dc:creator: Liam Denning

item.title: IRGC Letter to Americans Shows the Dark Thinking of Iran's Leaders
item.description: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has published a letter to the American people ahead of midterm elections in the US. Suffice to say that this remarkable document ends with Jesus Christ and the last Imam, Mahdi, rising together to lead humanity into the Kingdom of Heaven. I read all 14,390 words — think of it as a public service.
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion

item.title: Letterboxd’s Value Depends on Its Independence From Hollywood Studios
item.description: Letterboxd, once a niche social network for cinephiles to review, recommend and discover films, is now the subject of a potential nine-figure acquisition. As reported by the New York Times last week, the Canadian technology company Tiny is exploring selling its controlling stake in Letterboxd, with Sony Pictures, A24, and the Times itself expressing interest in a deal that could reach more than $300 million.
item.dc:creator: Miles Surrey

item.title: Florida Attorney General Uthmeier Is Too Busy Fighting Culture Wars
item.description: James Uthmeier, Florida’s attorney general, wants to be known as a politician who is all fight, all the time. The ambitious 38-year-old Georgetown law graduate considers himself the standard-bearer for the next generation of Republican culture warriors, and he’s using his office to make sure you notice.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: Federal Reserve’s Cost Overruns Expose Carelessness at the Top
item.description: The Federal Reserve’s internal watchdog found no evidence of criminal wrongdoing in the central bank’s $2.4 billion renovation of its Washington headquarters, which has run over budget and become a major flashpoint in President Donald Trump’s push to get policymakers to lower interest rates. item.title: Trump’s Foreign Policy Legacy at Halftime: Weakness Through War
item.description: With the congressional midterm elections nigh and the midpoint of Donald Trump’s second presidency not far behind, it’s time to ask: How does Trump’s foreign policy measure up so far? And where is it likely to go once he’s a lame duck?
item.dc:creator: Andreas Kluth
